# Real Coding-Agent Fit — DeepSeek V4 (Day 3)

**Last revised:** 2026-04-30
**Confidence:** Moderate. DeepSeek's own integration docs are explicit about three "blessed" tools and their env-var contracts. The bug-and-incompatibility picture is drawn from a single 19-completion GitHub issue, an open Cline PR, and an OpenRouter post that tested V3.1 — not V4 directly. Treat failure-rate numbers as point observations, not population statistics.

## Native V4 support vs BYOK-only

### Natively integrated (per DeepSeek's own coding-agents guide)

[`api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/coding_agents`](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/coding_agents) names exactly three tools:

1. Claude Code
2. OpenCode (≥ v1.14.24 to "avoid compatibility issues")
3. OpenClaw

The same page is explicit about exclusions: *"NOT mentioned in this guide: Aider, Cline, Continue, Cursor, Roo Code (community handles these via OpenAI-compatible BYOK)."* The April 24 release note repeats the short list with one omission: only Claude Code and OpenClaw appear in the news post; OpenCode is in the guide but not the announcement.

### BYOK via OpenAI-compatible endpoint

- **Cline** — PR #10401 (`feat(deepseek): Add deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro support`) was opened 2026-04-25 by `gerryqi` and was still **Open** as of 2026-04-27 ([source](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/10401)). 39 commits, JetBrains tests passing, but unmerged. Until merge, users wanting V4 in Cline today must either build from gerryqi's branch or use the generic OpenAI-compatible provider config pointing at `api.deepseek.com`.
- **Continue, Aider, Cursor, Roo Code** — none are addressed by DeepSeek; users wire them through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `api.deepseek.com`. Cursor and Roo Code carry an extra constraint — see the `reasoning_content` section below.

V4's release post says the API surfaces are stable: *"Keep base_url, just update model"* ([source](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news260424)). That is what enables the BYOK path at all.

## Claude Code integration

The smoothest path. DeepSeek publishes the exact env-var block:

```
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<DeepSeek API Key>
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=deepseek-v4-pro
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=deepseek-v4-pro
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=deepseek-v4-pro
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash
CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max
```

Two routing implications worth flagging:

1. `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash` — every internal Claude Code call that would have hit Haiku (file globs, lightweight classifiers, summarization passes) goes to V4-Flash. V4-Flash is carrying real load even when you think you're using V4-Pro.
2. `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash` — spawned subagents run on Flash, not Pro. The DeepSeek guide states this directly: *"Default model assignment in Claude Code: V4-Pro for primary work. V4-Flash for subagents."*

`CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max` pairs with the Anthropic-format effort contract: *"Anthropic format: `{\"output_config\": {\"effort\": \"high/max\"}}`. Default effort: high. Complex agent tasks auto-escalate to max."*

## The reasoning_content round-trip bug

The [thinking-mode docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode) define a strict contract that breaks naive OpenAI-compatible clients:

> "WITHOUT tool calls: previous turn's reasoning_content optional. 'Will be ignored by the API' if included."
>
> "WITH tool calls: reasoning_content 'must participate in the context concatenation and must be passed back to the API' in all subsequent turns."

The failure mode is explicit:

> "When tool calls occur and reasoning_content isn't properly passed back: the API will return a 400 error."

Clients that route assistant turns through OpenAI's standard schema generally drop `reasoning_content` because it is a DeepSeek-specific field. With tool-using sessions on V4-Pro, that drop is fatal.

**Workaround:** disable thinking mode entirely — `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` (the parameter "defaults to enabled"). You lose the reasoning quality but you stop hitting 400s. Note that thinking mode also rejects `temperature`, `top_p`, `presence_penalty`, and `frequency_penalty` — clients that always send those will see additional errors.

Per Counter-Discovery research, this incompatibility has been reported against **LiteLLM, OpenCode, Cursor, and Roo Code** — though direct issue confirmation for each was not in the pre-fetched material.

## The tool-call emission bug (V4-Pro)

[`github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3#1244`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3/issues/1244), filed **April 24, 2026** — V4 release day — documents V4-Pro intermittently emitting tool calls as plain text.

Single-session measurement (one 19-completion multi-turn run, ~40 tool definitions, official endpoint):

- 79% (15/19) correct `tool_calls` responses
- 11% (2/19) bug occurrences — function name + JSON arguments embedded in `content` string
- 10% (2/19) normal text replies (expected)

Buggy responses come back with `finish_reason: "stop"` and `tool_calls: null`. Direct quote from the issue: *"The model writes natural language first, then appends the tool name and raw JSON arguments directly into the content."* Buggy responses *"often begin with Chinese text ('thinking') before the tool call,"* and streaming usage fields show all zeros.

Issue status as of 2026-04-27: **Open. DeepSeek team response: NOT visible in fetched content. No fix status visible.**

n=19 is too small to claim 11% as a population rate, but it is the only public number, and the failure is reproducible enough to file. Agents that don't fall back to text-parsing tool calls will silently drop ~1 in 10 actions.

## Provider variance — OpenRouter Exacto

[`openrouter.ai/announcements/provider-variance-introducing-exacto`](https://openrouter.ai/announcements/provider-variance-introducing-exacto) (October 21, 2025) tested **DeepSeek 3.1**, not V4. The pattern is likely to carry forward; the numbers do not.

> "Significant variance in both tool-calling accuracy and propensity between providers hosting identical models."

Three measured failure modes: **invalid JSON returns, incorrect tool names, schema mismatches.** For DeepSeek 3.1: *"tight band of performance across providers — competitiveness even from Deepinfra (sole provider using fp4 quantization)."* Performance *"tend[s] to narrow as providers optimize inference stacks post-launch"* — meaning Day-3 V4 variance is likely worse than 3.1's mature state.

**Exacto routing** filters to providers meeting three criteria: top tool-calling accuracy, normal propensity ranges, low user-blacklist rates. Launched with five models including Kimi K2 and DeepSeek v3.1 Terminus; usage is `model_slug:exacto`. **No V4-Pro Exacto endpoint is documented yet.**

## Day-3 usability assessment

Honest read for an individual or small-team buyer in late April 2026:

1. **Claude Code is the only frictionless path.** DeepSeek publishes the env-var recipe and routes Anthropic-format effort directly. If you need V4 working on Day 3, install Claude Code and paste the block.
2. **Cline is PR-only as of April 27.** Either build from gerryqi's branch or use the OpenAI-compatible BYOK fallback.
3. **Cursor and Roo Code carry the `reasoning_content` incompatibility.** Workaround is disabling thinking mode, which forfeits V4-Pro's main reasoning advantage.
4. **V4-Pro silently emits ~11% of tool calls as plain text** in the one published measurement. No fix posted. Compounds the BYOK story: clients without tool-call-text fallback parsing will lose actions.
5. **Provider variance applies if you route through OpenRouter or aggregators.** Use `:exacto` slugs where available, accept that V4-Pro doesn't have one yet, and prefer the official DeepSeek endpoint for tool-heavy workloads.

The release card hands you a 1.6T-param model with `LiveCodeBench 93.5%`, `SWE Verified 80.6%`, `Terminal Bench 2.0 67.9%`. The integration story does not yet match the model story. Day 3 is "Claude Code with DeepSeek's env block, or wait."

One tokenizer footnote that may bite custom integrations: the V4-Pro model card states *"Chat template: No Jinja format. Uses dedicated `encoding_dsv4` Python module."* Anything that templates DeepSeek prompts via Jinja will need updating. OpenAI-format users at `api.deepseek.com` are insulated because the server handles it.
